evals.prompt: Acme's monthly churn on the Starter plan went from 2.1% in July to 3.4% in August. Theories: the price rise from $19 to $24 on 1 Aug, a new competitor (Northwind Lite) launching in late July, or the onboarding email sequence that broke on 20 Jul. Evidence: churn rose on monthly and annual-renewal customers alike; cancellation survey 'too expensive' share went from 30% to 32%; customers who signed up after 20 Jul churn at 5.8%, older cohorts at 2.4%; win-back calls mention Northwind Lite twice out of 40. Which explanation fits best and what should we check next?
assertions: Lists at least four rival hypotheses, including a measurement or definition hypothesis the user did not raise
Builds a matrix rating every evidence item against every hypothesis as consistent, inconsistent or neutral (or CC/II/NA)
Ranks hypotheses by how much evidence contradicts them, not by how much supports them, and shows the scores or arithmetic
Names the non-diagnostic evidence (rated the same for every hypothesis) and does not use it as support
Names the linchpin evidence whose removal would change the leader, or states that none exists
Gives the conclusion a confidence word with a reason
Names one next observation that the top two hypotheses predict differently, with the result each predicts
Does not invent evidence, numbers or sources that are not in the prompt; anything inferred is tagged [assumption]

evals.prompt: Our honey harvest crashed this year and my partner and I disagree about why. Everything we know is in season_notes.md. Answer the question in the notes. One page.
assertions: Reports the drop as about 27% (3,150 kg to 2,300 kg), catching that the owner's '40%' does not match the yard data
Notes that the Hilltop yard's yield was essentially unchanged, so the loss is concentrated at Riverside and Orchard, contradicting 'every hive was hit the same'
Treats mite counts below the treatment threshold in every yard as evidence against varroa as the main cause, and does not endorse the $4,000 treatment programme on the strength of the mite theory
Does not claim the pesticide explanation is proven or enough on its own for a lawyer's letter, and says what is missing
Names a next observation that would separate the leading explanations, such as residue testing of the frozen bag of dead bees
Does not invent evidence (lab results, product names, spray dates) not in the notes
Fits about one page

evals.prompt: so our village pub's sunday lunch trade has really dropped since about june. my husband says its the new chef, i reckon its the road works on the high street, our daughter says its because we put prices up. we did all three around the same time lol. few bullets on how to work out which one it actually is?
assertions: Answers in a few bullets — no more than about 10 bullets or 250 words — without asking questions first
Weighs all three explanations and does not declare a winner without evidence
Points out that because the three changes happened at about the same time, timing alone cannot tell them apart

Suggests specific, cheap checks the pub can do that would point to one explanation over the others (for example whether weekday or drinks-only trade also fell, whether regulars still come but spend less, what reviews say about the food, or what happens when the road works end)
Does not invent sales figures, dates, or customer feedback not given
Plain language with no analysis jargon
